repeatability.caveats: N=5 makes the CV estimate itself noisy - read the raw per-repeat numbers in results.csv (committed) and the committed run records under records/, not just the CV summary. Wall times were recorded under fleet load (6 concurrent lanes during these runs) and are load-affected facts, not rankable meters. This is per-goban-independent (a measurement of the cost instruments, not of the engine); no goban claim is proposed.
repeatability.design: T626's score-spread race applied to cost. 4 cells = 2 models (deepseek-v4-flash = DeepSeek lane, claude-opus-5 = Claude lane) x 2 brief shapes (M = short mechanical census, A = long read-only audit). N=5 independent repeats per cell, 20 runs total, byte-identical sealed briefs, fresh context per repeat, frozen worktree at 2ec4f93 reset before every run. Interleaved order; every repeat launched under tools/runner (the ordinary-lane wrapper) with run records + token capture. Meters: total tokens = tokens_in + tokens_out (the cost ladder's own unit); cpu-seconds and peak rss_mb from the runner; wall recorded as fact (load-affected, not rankable). Controls (null + seeded + negative + runner smoke) ran before any live reading.
repeatability.question: When the same model runs the same sealed brief repeatedly in fresh contexts, how much do total tokens, cpu-seconds, and peak rss move, and is the spread small enough for cost to re-enter model selection?
repeatability.recommendation: Cost does NOT re-enter model selection. The gate is NOT passed: the ladder's own unit (total tokens) measures CV 3-7x the 0.05 rankability bar on every cell, and the spread is intrinsic (provider prompt-cache nondeterminism + per-run reasoning variance) rather than N=5 sampling noise - the per-cell range is 0.8-1.4x the mean. cpu-seconds fails worse. Only peak rss is repeatable, and only on the short mechanical brief; at most rss-on-M could feed a per-shape REPORTING band, never a selection decision. T772 (or its successor) should keep cost as a reporting surface only, per the ratified direction.

thresholds.rule: CV <= 0.05: rankable with confidence. 0.05 < CV <= 0.15: rankable only for gaps >= 2x the cell sd (consumer must carry mean +/- 2sd and require band-disjointness). CV > 0.15: not rankable.

cpu_seconds.read: NOT rankable. CV 0.11-0.58; the expensive A brief on the Claude lane is the worst cell (0.576, driven by a 7.8s outlier against 2.7-3.4s).

fresh_vs_cache.read: Fresh tokens (the actual compute, the part that costs money) are also not rankable at 0.05 (CV 0.07-0.27). The fresh/cache split differs by ~1000x between families on the A brief - Claude serves ~99.99% from cache (fresh ~76 tokens/run) while DeepSeek re-reads ~75k fresh tokens/run - so a cross-family TOTAL-token comparison is additionally meaningless without the split, corroborating T746 3.3's '>10x' ruling.

peak_rss.read: The only meter that clears the 0.05 bar, and only on the short mechanical brief (CV 0.005-0.014). On the A brief it drops to the band zone (CV 0.09-0.13).

total_tokens.read: The cost ladder's own unit is NOT rankable. CV ranges 0.14-0.34 across the four cells (3-7x the 0.05 bar). Three cells fail outright (>0.15); the best cell (op-a, 0.141) is only in the band zone, and its band [2.30M, 4.11M] already contains ds-a's mean (2.35M) - so no two models separate on total tokens even in the best case.
